properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-10-24: "null unsets everywhere": extend the 09-07 rule to every typed constructor, as its OWN later PR.

THE CASE. The Shop sample trial (2026-10-24): `limit: null` on add_constraint was ignored, so a numeric limit could not be cleared once set. Measured on main 61c05ad74: the typed request takes the limit as an optional number, so null and absent are the same, and the write merges. The 2026-09-07 rule (chg:eight-field-feedback-fixes-land-for-v0510: "A null UNSETS rather than being refused") was built into create_node's props bag only. The class: a rule settled at one door and never reached the others. Not built on PR #795; it is its own later PR.

BUILT 2026-10-24 on feat/null-unsets-on-every-typed-constructor (chg:a-null-unsets-at-every-typed-constructor-2026-10-24): every add_* constructor, plan_epoch and record_finding unset an optional property sent as null and name it under `unset`; a null on a required field (the schema's, or one the constructor needs to create the node) is refused by name; a field left out keeps its value. Pinned by ver:a-null-unsets-at-every-typed-constructor-tests over the served surface.

RULED 2026-10-25, Anthony, on PR #797's three open points: "Go with your recommendation on null unsets". (1) A null on `distinct_from`, or on any field the schema keeps as ADDITIVE history, is REFUSED by name and nothing is written: history is not erased by a null. (2) A null on a `status` is REFUSED by name, nothing is written, and the refusal names the matching `set_*_status` tool: a null never silently resets a status to its default. (3) A client sending null for every empty field clears those fields; the changelog fragment says so plainly, as a behaviour change MCP clients should know about. Built on the same branch (nulls.rs refuse_history_and_status), pinned by ver:a-null-unsets-at-every-typed-constructor-tests.
